Thanks for submitting Redwood for our platform RFP. The security team has a short vulnerability-management appendix we need answered for vendor selection. Top items we need clarified:

Kim / Laura — sharing the technical pieces below; I kept this focused so it can slot into the one-pagers.

SAST/DAST
- SAST: We run Snyk and internal static analysis during PR gating; weekly incremental scans for main branches, full-scan on release. Findings are triaged in Jira and tracked to remediation.
- DAST: We run scheduled DAST on staging for major services (monthly) and ad-hoc scans before production rollouts. Results feed into the same Jira workflow.
- CI gating: High/critical SAST findings block merge until triaged; DAST findings generate EPICs for remediation as per severity.

Patch SLA matrix (summary)
- Critical (RCE, auth bypass): deployable patch availability target = 48 hours; customer-deploy guidance and hotfix within 72 hours if hosted; for Private, we publish patch and mitigations within 48 hours and provide backport if requested.
- High: patch availability target = 7 days; recommended customer deploy within 14 days.
- Medium: patch availability target = 30 days.
- Low: next maintenance window / scheduled release.
Notes: SLA refers to time-to-patch-availability (when vendor-provided patch or mitigations are published). Customer deployment timelines vary depending on Dedicated/Private. We will provide a detailed Excel matrix as an attachment.

Pen test summary
- Last third-party external pen test completed: 2027-05-04 (scope: hosted API endpoint, auth flows, serving runtime).
- We can provide a redacted executive summary and remediation tracker; full raw report requires an NDA and additional redaction. Attached: pentest-exec-summary-2027-05.pdf (redacted).

SBOM
- We generate SBOMs per build for all customer-facing images (CycloneDX format CSV/JSON available). Hosted and Dedicated: full SBOMs provided. Private (customer-managed on-prem): we produce the SBOM package and will provide it to the customer for their internal supply-chain processes. Sample attached: SBOM_manifest_20270531.csv

Attachments (will include in packet): pentest-exec-summary-2027-05.pdf (redacted exec summary), SBOM_manifest_20270531.csv, patch-sla-matrix.xlsx.

I'll attach the XLSX and the one-pagers by EOD Monday.

— Priyom
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Priyom — that's helpful. A couple quick clarifications before you finalize: 

1) For the patch SLA: when you say "patch availability" — do you mean vendor release (artifact published) or the time to a hosted automatic patch? We need the distinction for scoring.
2) For pen test artifacts: exec summary is fine. For the scoring committee, would a signed letter from the pen-test vendor confirming scope and remediation closure be acceptable in place of the full report?

Also, can you confirm the file formats (we prefer CycloneDX or SPDX for SBOM) and whether the SBOM includes non-code dependencies (OS packages, third-party libs)?

If you can answer these two bullets and get the packet over by Monday EOD that will keep us on schedule.

Laura

Laura — quick answers and final delivery plan: 

1) Patch SLA language: our matrix will explicitly separate (a) "vendor-published patch availability" (time from CVE/public disclosure to vendor-published fix) and (b) "hosted auto-deploy window" (for Redwood Hosted endpoints we maintain an automated hotfix pipeline with a target rollout within 24–72 hours for critical fixes). Private/Dedicated deployments: we publish patch artifacts and mitigations; we do not auto-apply. The attached patch-sla-matrix.xlsx has separate columns for both items with targets per severity.

2) Pen test evidence: a signed letter from the 3rd-party pentest vendor confirming scope and remediation status is acceptable for scoring. We will include the redacted executive summary plus a signed attestation from the vendor. Full unredacted reports can be provided under our standard MSA/NDA process.

3) SBOM: we will provide CycloneDX CSV and JSON exports; SBOMs include OS packages, language packages, and direct transitive dependencies for the artifacts in scope. A sample (SBOM_manifest_20270531.csv) is attached.

Delivery plan: one-pagers + XLSX + two attached artifacts (redacted exec summary, SBOM CSV) will be uploaded to the Drive link and shared with your security mailbox by EOD Monday (2027-06-14). We will send the vendor attestation soon after. If you prefer we can also upload to the HubSpot record for your procurement team — see link below.

Links: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/ACD-2027-045 (evidence tab)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Acadia-RFP-evidence

Let me know if there's anything else — we aim to make this as frictionless as possible.
